items.text: Hossein Aghaei, a member of Iran International's editorial team, said that the exchange of letters between JD Vance and Mohsen Rezaee is a normal part of diplomacy but is unlikely to lead to constructive negotiations. He added that the political deadlock in Israel and the approaching US midterm elections may not diminish the military option. It is also possible that Netanyahu uses this situation to persuade the Trump administration to take military action against the Islamic Republic.

Stephen Curry, the 38-year-old Golden State superstar, scored 44 points in a 119-114 victory over Minnesota, marking his fifteenth 40-point game after age 35 and matching LeBron James' historic record. Curry had an exceptional performance in this game, and Golden State's coach said Curry can always change the course of the game. Despite Golden State's 24-point lead at one point, Minnesota did not give up, and Curry had to play close to the 32-minute limit set for his time on the court.

Rahman Amouzad, Iran's 65 kg freestyle wrestling representative, lost 3-2 to Vazgen Tovanyan from Armenia in the quarterfinals of the World Championships and failed to advance to the semifinals. Amouzad, like Hassan Yazdani, lost the match in the final seconds. He must wait for Tovanyan to reach the final to return to the competition through the repechage group and compete for a bronze medal.

Messages and reports received by Iran International indicate an increase in food prices, including bread, chicken, meat, and tea. Citizens say the rising food prices have made it difficult for many people to meet their daily needs.

With over 91% of the votes counted in the Israeli parliamentary elections, neither Benjamin Netanyahu nor Gadi Eizenkot has achieved the majority needed to form a government. Four scenarios facing Israel include forming a national unity government, an opposition coalition supported by Arab parties, right-wing parties joining Netanyahu's coalition, or holding early elections. Reza Mohaddes, a reporter for Iran International, examines these scenarios and the obstacles facing each.

Nabi Omidi, a dismissed associate professor of economics and financial management at Payame Noor University, was sentenced to 9 years in prison by the Ilam Province Court of Appeal. This sentence had previously been issued by the Ilam Revolutionary Court and was confirmed as is in the appeal stage. He was convicted on charges including acting against national security, propaganda against the regime, and participating in protests, with 5 years of the sentence enforceable under Article 134 of the Islamic Penal Code.

Hebrew media reported that Shin Bet, Israel's internal security agency, is investigating the possibility of money transfers from abroad, including Qatar and Turkey, to organizations encouraging electoral participation in the Arab community in Israel. This investigation began after the head of the Central Elections Committee requested a probe into Likud party allegations of foreign funding and possible electoral bribery.

The European Union representative at the Third Committee of the UN General Assembly announced that since December 1404, the EU has sanctioned 37 individuals and 9 entities for human rights violations in Iran. The representative expressed concern over the suppression of the December 1404 protests, use of deadly force, increased arbitrary arrests, torture, and executions. They also called for an end to executions, release of arbitrarily detained individuals, and accountability for human rights violators.

Omid Faraghat, a journalist imprisoned in the Central Prison of Karaj, was sentenced by the second branch of the Revolutionary Court of this city to 10 years and one day in prison, permanent dismissal from government and public services, and two years of prohibition from journalistic activity.

Hassan Yazdani, captain of Iran's freestyle wrestling team, was defeated by Arash Yoshida, an Iranian-Japanese wrestler, in the round of 16 at the World Championships. Rahman Amouzad also failed to reach the semifinals after losing to an opponent from Armenia. An interview was conducted with sports reporter Mehdi Rostampour.

The online media "Azad" announced the lifting of restrictions and resumption of its activities after about two months of suspension by judicial order. This media had previously been banned from publishing new programs following a criminal complaint by the Tehran prosecutor's office.

The Spanish Football Federation fined Barcelona 602 euros after Atletico Madrid complained about negotiations to sign Julian Alvarez. The disciplinary committee considered the act a minor violation and imposed the maximum fine. Barcelona denied any wrongdoing and plans to appeal.

Amir Mohammad Najafi was killed on 18 Dey in Fardis Karaj by gunfire from the suppressive forces of the Islamic Republic. His name remains in the memory of this land and his memory is a guiding light for freedom seekers.

Videos received by Iran International show that a group of Iranians residing in Canada gathered on Wednesday, 6 Aban, in front of the CBC media office in Halifax and demanded media coverage of the crimes of the Islamic Republic.

Morteza Kazemian, a member of Iran International's editorial team, said the simultaneous emphasis by Donald Trump on "finishing the work of the Islamic Republic" and the sending of a letter from JD Vance to Mohsen Rezaei indicates that communication channels between Washington and Tehran remain open. According to Kazemian, this letter could be the last diplomatic effort by the US to reach an agreement, but disagreements over the Islamic Republic's nuclear program, the Strait of Hormuz, and support for proxy forces have clouded the prospects for an agreement and increased the risk of war.

Student and youth organizations in France continue to plan protests. Restrictions on gatherings and possible curfews have intensified the debate about the right to protest in the country. In Germany, after the announcement of far-left groups joining the demonstrations, police officials have warned about the possibility of violent actions.

The New York Times reported that direct negotiations between Tehran and Washington may begin next week in Qatar or Turkey. If Tehran accepts JD Vance's proposal letter, negotiations will technically start without preconditions, but Iran's nuclear program must be on the table. The report also mentioned diplomatic efforts by regional countries to reduce tensions and concerns about the risk of war.

Amin Ghanbari, a journalist from Semnan and manager of the Telegram channel "Payamgou-ye Semnan," has been sentenced to 20 years in prison by the first branch of the Revolutionary Court of that city. The charges against Ghanbari include "media action against the Islamic Republic," "assembly and collusion," "propaganda activity against the regime," "support for Pahlavi and the victims of Dey 1404 protests," and "insulting the founder of the Islamic Republic." Ghanbari was arrested in front of his house in Ordibehesht this year, and no details about the case, evidence, or his place of detention have been released.

A judge in Italy ordered the release of Youssef Sihr, a journalist and activist accused of inciting violence in Milan protests. Sihr, whom police identified as the administrator of the "October 17 Movement" Telegram group, was arrested on October 24 on charges of incitement to commit crimes with terrorist aims. Giorgia Meloni, Italy's Prime Minister, called his release "shameful" and humiliating for the police and investigators.

Israel held five parliamentary elections in less than four years from 2019 to 2022; a period marked by deadlock in forming a government, the formation and collapse of coalitions, and the return of Benjamin Netanyahu to power. Now, if parties do not reach an agreement to form a government, there is a possibility of holding elections again.
A video published on social media shows a group of customers of Saipa automotive company gathering due to delays in the delivery of Shahin Plus and regular Shahin cars.

IRNA reported on the occupational and livelihood challenges of environmental guards. Shortage of personnel, salaries not matching living costs, and uncertainty about employment status are among their main problems. The commander of the Environmental Protection Unit emphasized the need to provide equipment and improve the working conditions of environmental guards.

Houshang Seydali, the coordination manager of the National Iranian Gas Company, announced that gas supply conditions for the upcoming winter have become more difficult and planning has been done to provide alternative fuels such as gas cylinders and kerosene. He said about 11 provinces may face gas shortages, with three northern provinces having more difficult conditions. Seydali considered electricity the best option for home energy supply, provided sufficient electricity can be produced.
The public and revolutionary prosecutor of South Khorasan announced the closure of three cafes in Birjand due to violations related to religious regulations and public decency.

A group of Spanish citizens clashed with police in Madrid on Wednesday, 6 Aban, protesting against the government after a deadly train collision. About 500 people gathered in front of the Ministry of Transport and threw bottles and incendiary materials at the police. Officers used tear gas to disperse the protesters.

The Intelligence Department of Sistan and Baluchestan Province reported the arrest of 19 people in the central and southern counties of the province. According to this security agency, some of the detainees had connections with the US and Israel and were involved in the killing of several law enforcement officers in Iranshahr county. Three others are accused of collecting and sending information about defense and security centers.

Stopping or delays in the passage of more than four thousand trucks at the Iran-Turkey borders and the increase in maritime transport costs have raised concerns about the transfer of goods and the supply of essential needs of the people. The head of the Transport Commission of the Tehran Chamber of Commerce said the cost of transporting a 40-foot container from China has risen from about $2,700 to $2,800 to $13,600. Reports of similar problems on the routes of Iraq and Pakistan have also been raised.

Viviana Krsticic, a member of the UN fact-finding mission on Iran, stated that based on the mission's findings, many human rights violations by officials and institutions of the Islamic Republic in Iran during 2026 constitute crimes against humanity. She mentioned arbitrary arrests, torture, sexual violence, denial of fair trial, and arbitrary deprivation of the right to life. Switzerland condemns the use of the death penalty and emphasizes support for halting executions and protecting human rights defenders.

The death sentence of Leila Abolhasani, a 43-year-old citizen and detainee from the December 1404 protests, was overturned by the Supreme Court and her case was returned to the court for retrial. She had previously been sentenced to death by the Fifth Branch of the Isfahan Revolutionary Court on charges of "moharebeh" (waging war against God). This sentence overturn followed an appeal by her lawyer.
On Thursday, 7 Aban around 16:00, it was reported that a large fire occurred on the Tehran-Karaj highway. Received images from citizens show this incident.

On the occasion of the 7th of Aban, the day commemorating Cyrus, a citizen told Iran International that this day is a reminder of a civilization's glory rooted deep in the history of this land and a day of a man whose name is intertwined with the greatness of Iran.

Moloud Hajizadeh, an economic journalist, said some households had previously replaced rice with bread, but now they have no substitute for bread either. He added that continuing this trend could turn bread supply for lower income groups into a crisis and expand livelihood protests.

A video received by Iran International on Thursday, 7 Aban, shows a large fire in a building at kilometer 11 of Karaj Special Road. It is said that the burning building belongs to Tehran Darou Company.

The Islamic Republic has again this year, as in the past decade, banned people's presence at the historical site of Pasargadae on Cyrus Day and restricted the routes leading to Cyrus's tomb. Despite these restrictions, Iran International's audience said that the name Cyrus has become a point of identity and a symbol for recalling the right to freedom and human dignity.

Tehran Revolutionary Court sentenced three detainees of the December 1404 protests to death. Amir Reza Rezaei, Vahid Ghahramani, and a cleric named Mehdi were sentenced on charges of operational action for Israel. Mehdi was also sentenced to death in a separate case by the Special Clerical Court for apostasy.

Reports include paying 500,000 tomans subsidy for buying bread and pickles compared to house prices in 1979 in Kermanshah. Employees of Atlas Air have not received several months of salaries, and prices of motor oil and the drug Fluphenazine have sharply increased. Some bakeries are accused of methods to sell government-subsidized flour on the free market.

Andy Burnham, the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, announced that the country is making every effort to reduce tensions and help fully reopen the Strait of Hormuz amid the consequences of the Iran war. He said he spoke with Donald Trump last week about the situation in the Strait of Hormuz. Burnham emphasized that this process must occur without any nuclear capabilities in Iran.

Dmitry Peskov, Kremlin spokesperson, announced that Russia is ready to mediate between the Islamic Republic and the United States if requested. He said the issue of Iran is always raised in Moscow-Washington contacts and Russia wants to prevent military conflict in the Persian Gulf. Peskov also stated that if the dispute is over Iran's enriched uranium, Moscow is ready to transfer it to Russian territory.

Informed sources told Iran International that 10 plainclothes agents raided the homes of Raouf Rouhani Najafabadi, his mother Ferdows Ferdousian, and his mother-in-law Forough Darab in Isfahan on November 5, confiscating a large number of their belongings over six hours. According to these sources, the masked agents confiscated 9 mobile phones, 3 televisions, 3 laptops, a home theater system, several cameras, 4 musical instruments, over 15 suitcases and bags, over 30 million tomans in cash, all gold and jewelry, and some other items. A few days before this raid, Raouf Rouhani Najafabadi's wife had received an SMS from Article 49 Court, which is related to property confiscation and the "Headquarters for Executing Imam Khomeini's Order."

Tasnim reported that the trip of Tractor Tabriz football team to Oman for the match against Neftchi Uzbekistan in the Asian Elite League has become uncertain due to the flight permit not being issued. The team is scheduled to host Neftchi in Oman on Monday, 11 Aban in the fourth week of the Asian Elite League, but the flight permit has not yet been issued. Javad Nekounam warned that if another long trip is forced, the youth team will participate instead of the main team.

Branch 23 of Tehran Revolutionary Court sentenced Amir Reza Rezaei, Vahid Ghahremani, and Mehdi, a cleric whose last name was not announced, three detainees of the January 2026 protests, to death. Harana reported that this sentence was communicated to the three prisoners in prison on Monday, October 26. The charges against them include "operational action for Israel."
A citizen sent a video to Iran International showing disturbances to people and traffic caused by government protesters.

A citizen reported that on the day of commemorating Cyrus, they were inspected more than 10 times on the route from Yazd to Shiraz and were not allowed to enter Pasargadae. He said Cyrus's value lies in his intellectual and human legacy, not just in conquests. He also referred to the importance of Cyrus Day as a symbol of management combined with humanity and a reminder of concepts such as tolerance and human rights.

Israel's Likud party called for police and Shin Bet involvement in the election manipulation case and announced it will present hundreds of testimonies and evidence for review. The party claimed foreign entities intervened in the elections by bribing voters to change the balance of power in the Knesset and remove the right-wing government. Meanwhile, Israeli police announced the arrest of seven more people suspected of election bribery in favor of the Arab party Ra'am.

The United Nations reported in its latest report that opium production in Afghanistan has increased fivefold. The report states that opium production in 2026 has reached nearly 1500 tons, about five times that of the previous year.

Heavy rains and flooding in various parts of Syria have killed at least two people and forced hundreds of families to leave their homes. Syrian officials reported that seven bridges and communication routes have become inaccessible, and the flood has damaged homes and refugee camps. Warnings about continued rainfall and the possibility of flooding remain in place.

A report states that three citizens from Baneh, including two 17-year-old teenagers named Ilya Lotfi Tormakchi and Zhiyar Rasouli, and an 18-year-old named Mohammad Faraji, remain in indefinite detention in a security detention center in Sanandaj despite 10 days having passed since their arrest.

On Tuesday, 5 Aban, security forces simultaneously searched the homes of three Baháʼí families in Isfahan. During the search, numerous personal belongings and properties including 9 mobile phones, three televisions, three laptops, a home cinema system, over 30 million tomans in cash, and jewelry were confiscated. Additionally, two bracelets belonging to the wife of one of the citizens were forcibly removed with pliers.

According to information received by Iran International, the mothers of Ali Alavi and Saeed Najafi, who are among the martyrs of the Dey protests, died less than 10 months after their sons were killed. Ali Alavi, 35 years old, was killed on 19 Dey in Fardis, Karaj, and Saeed Najafi, 34 years old, was killed on 18 Dey in Naziabad, Tehran by suppression forces. More details in an interview with Farnoush Faraji, a member of the Iran International editorial team.

Saad Sherida Al-Kaabi, CEO of Qatar Energy, said he met twice in the past two weeks with the acting Iranian Oil Minister and both sides are exploring oil and gas cooperation after the war ends. Al-Kaabi said Qatar Energy is buying long-term liquefied natural gas from the US and other suppliers to offset losses from the Iran war and protect its revenues against possible disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz. He added these purchases are part of Qatar Energy's strategy to hedge commercial risks and exploit price differences in the global gas market.
Mehrangiz Rastin, a resident of Kohgiluyeh and Boyer-Ahmad province, has been arrested by security agencies.
An emergency technician in Sanandaj was assaulted and injured by a patient's companion while providing medical services.

The prison sentence of Fatemeh Mojaddad, a political prisoner and detainee from the January 1404 protests, was converted to a suspended sentence. She will serve the remainder of her sentence outside of Varamin Qarchak prison. Fatemeh Mojaddad was released from prison on Wednesday, 6 Aban.

Kyriakos Mitsotakis, Prime Minister of Greece, on Thursday, 7 Aban, called for a global ceasefire in maritime transport and stated that attacks on civilian commercial ships are unacceptable and threaten international trade and security. He said at a UN Security Council meeting that commercial ships should be able to navigate freely and safely even during military conflicts. Mitsotakis added that disruption of shipping freedom increases costs and instability in global markets.

Imran Amani, a 21-year-old prisoner held in Greater Tehran Prison and one of the detainees of the Dey 1404 protests, was sentenced to death by Branch 26 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court on charges of "waging war against God". The sentence was issued by Branch 26 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court headed by Judge Iman Afshari and was communicated to this prisoner on Saturday, 2 Aban.

Ali Sadrozadeh, a Middle East analyst, considered Netanyahu's coalition with opposition parties difficult and said that the occurrence of a war with the Islamic Republic could change the calculations of government formation.

Reuters reported that Julita Gaigo, a 24-year-old Spanish long jump athlete, was one of the victims of a deadly collision between two high-speed trains in Toledo province, Spain. The Spanish Athletics Federation confirmed her death and expressed condolences to her family and teammates. The incident killed at least 69 people and was the second deadly accident in less than a year on the rail line connecting Madrid to southern Andalusia.

The British newspaper Telegraph reported that after attempting to interfere in Israel's elections, the Islamic Republic is preparing operations to disrupt the US midterm elections. Iranian officials said Tehran's goal is to create political division and deadlock in the US and Israel. It was also reported that powerful cyber groups have been formed to hack their electoral systems.

After the final results of the Israeli parliamentary elections were announced, the process of forming a new government begins; a process that, given that none of the main coalitions reached the majority of 61 Knesset seats, may involve lengthy negotiations among parties and even lead to new elections.

The Israeli election committee announced the completion of counting all votes, including double-envelope ballots, and said it will soon publish the final results. According to the published results, Netanyahu's coalition has 53 seats, opposition parties 48, and Arab parties 19 seats; Likud is also the largest Knesset party with 26 seats.
A citizen sent a video to Iran International showing cut trees on Tehranser Boulevard in western Tehran and said: "They have attacked the city's trees."

London City Club, which started its activity with women's football, now has Alexia Putellas, a three-time Ballon d'Or winner, in its squad. Raha Pourbakhsh, an Iran International reporter, narrates the fan culture in women's football on the sidelines of this team's match against Crystal Palace.

Jewish Chronicle reported that the US is transferring a Patriot missile defense system from Texas to the Middle East. This move comes as Washington prepares for the possibility of resuming military attacks against the Islamic Republic after the US midterm elections on November 3. Donald Trump has not yet made a final decision about new attacks on Iran.

Yair Golan, leader of the Israeli Democratic Party, wrote after meeting Gadi Eizenkot, leader of the Yashar party, that both have dedicated many years to Israel's security and that saving Israel is the main issue. This meeting took place after the parliamentary elections and Golan's meeting with Yair Lapid. Golan emphasized that they are partners in the commitment to ensure a better future for Israel.

Zakaria Naroui, an 18-year-old resident of Bazman County, was arrested by intelligence officers in this county on 5 Mehr. Since the arrest, there has been no information about the place of detention of this citizen.

An informed Iranian source told Al Mayadeen that JD Vance, the US Vice President, recently exchanged messages with Mohsen Rezaei, Secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council. The source emphasized that Iran will take no new action before implementing its seven conditions, which must be implemented all at once. Tehran is also concerned that removing enriched materials from the country might pave the way for a new US military attack instead of ending the war.

The United States Central Command (CENTCOM) on Thursday, 7 Aban, rejected the claim by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps about seizing a US "spy and deception" drone. Team Hawkins, CENTCOM spokesperson, said the IRGC has repeatedly lied in recent weeks and months and today is no different. Earlier the IRGC claimed to have seized a US "MQM-170" drone in the western Strait of Hormuz.

Moharram Navidkia, head coach of Sepahan, said in a press conference before the match against Kheybar Khorramabad that the football quality of the Iranian Premier League is not very high and the close points of the top 5 teams do not mean the league quality is high. He added that this issue can be seen in clubs and national teams from youth to senior levels.

The death sentence of Mohammad Naderi, a prisoner in Qezel Hesar prison in Karaj who was convicted of espionage, was confirmed by the Supreme Court. This sentence was previously issued by Branch 23 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court. Harana reported that Naderi is held in Unit 3, Hall 37 of Qezel Hesar prison.

Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar party, accused Benjamin Netanyahu and the Likud party of launching an organized campaign to discredit the election results and said he would not allow any disruption in the inauguration of the new parliament. He also called foreign interference in Israeli elections unacceptable and mentioned investigating Qatar's role. Eisenkot spoke about plans for military and public service and forming a commission to investigate the October 7 attacks.

A citizen sent a video to Iran International saying the economic situation of people in Iran has become very weak. He said that he and his wife are both employed but even with 100 million tomans per month they cannot make a living. For this reason, they are forced to end his wife's pregnancy.

Donald Trump said JD Vance's contact with Tehran was about providing medical aid and equipment. Tasnim News Agency confirmed Vance's letter to the Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council of the Islamic Republic and wrote that no response has been given yet.

Senior Canadian security officials warned that threats against the Jewish community in the country have reached an unprecedented level. According to them, this community faces a range of threats, including violent extremism and threatening activities by the Islamic Republic.

Cristiano Ronaldo thanked football fans worldwide after his 2008 Ballon d'Or was chosen as the best Ballon d'Or of all time. France Football introduced a new award called "BOAT" to select the best Ballon d'Or in history, with magazine users voting instead of journalists. Ronaldo's 2008 Ballon d'Or ranked first in this poll.

Times of Israel reported that an Israeli soldier was arrested on charges of spying for the Islamic Republic and transferring sensitive military information in exchange for cryptocurrency. The soldier, arrested in September, had been in contact with Islamic Republic intelligence agents for about a year and provided information about his unit's activities and the readiness of the Israeli army. The Israeli military prosecutor stated that the soldier also sent information about military bases and photos of interceptor systems and military vehicles.

Mehdi Taj, the head of the Football Federation, said in response to reporters about negotiations with Gianni Infantino, the FIFA president, for the return of hosting Iranian teams in Asia, that the most important issue is their blocked funds and he asked him to think about it. Taj stated they currently have a claim of 20 million dollars. He left further questions about negotiations and consultations for the return of hosting unanswered.

Milad Ebrahimi, a citizen from Kamyaran and one of the injured in the December 1404 protests, was sentenced by Branch 101 of the Criminal Court Two of this city to one year in prison and a fine of 400 million tomans.

Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, Speaker of the Islamic Consultative Assembly, wrote on X on Thursday, 7 Aban, that the conditions of the Islamic Republic have been clearly communicated to mediators multiple times, and progress in negotiations will only be possible if Tehran's seven conditions are accepted. Ghalibaf emphasized that the carrot and stick approach has no effect on Tehran, and progress will only be achieved when the seven conditions of the Islamic Republic are accepted.

Reuters reported that American oil companies ExxonMobil and Chevron have canceled their senior executives' trips to the ADIPEC oil and gas exhibition in Abu Dhabi due to security concerns over potential new US attacks on Iran and Tehran's retaliatory response. Darren Woods, CEO of ExxonMobil, and Kayne Nelson, head of Chevron's upstream division, were scheduled to attend the event. This decision was made amid concerns that potential renewed US attacks on Iran and the Islamic Republic's military response have affected oil markets.
The UK Maritime Trade Operations center reported that a tanker belonging to a shipping company was hit by an unidentified projectile while passing through the Strait of Hormuz.

Today, Thursday 7 Aban, Shahin vehicle voucher holders protested in front of Saipa. They are protesting the non-delivery of their registered vehicles despite payment and the passing of announced deadlines.

Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, Speaker of the Islamic Consultative Assembly, stated that Iran's conditions have been explicitly communicated to mediators multiple times. He said that the carrot and stick approach has no effect on Iran, and progress can only be achieved if Iran's seven conditions are agreed upon.
A prisoner in Lordegan County who had previously been sentenced to death was spared from execution due to the forgiveness of the victim's family.

Varzesh3 reported that Alireza Dabir, head of the Wrestling Federation, took Rahman Amouzad to a sauna for two hours to lose weight after the Armenian wrestler reached the world championship final. Amouzad's weight suddenly increased after his first match, which he lost. After about six hours and before preparing for night rest, Amouzad reached the ideal weight.

Somayeh Afshar, the mother of Alireza Sepahi whose execution was carried out in Mehr, is serving a five-year prison sentence in Dolatabad Prison in Isfahan. She was sentenced by the First Branch of the Revolutionary Court of Isfahan in a case related to the protests of Dey 1404. Somayeh Afshar was arrested about 20 days after her son was detained in Bahman 1404.

Israel held five parliamentary elections between 1398 and 1401 in less than four years. If efforts to form a government fail after the final election results are announced, the legal process can take up to about 120 days. If the deadlock continues, new elections could be held in spring 1406.
On the occasion of the 7th of Aban, a citizen said that the image of Cyrus goes beyond the founder of an empire and he symbolizes noble traits such as tolerance, generosity, courage, and boldness.

Messages from Qeshm report hearing the sound of a missile launch and a fighter jet flying at low altitude at 22:48. The sounds of fighter jets and missile launches are often confused. A received photo indicates that it was a projectile launch.

The Wall Street Journal reported that Brad Cooper, commander of CENTCOM, presented military options against the Islamic Republic to Donald Trump in a meeting at the White House. The meeting took place as Washington is considering the possibility of resuming large-scale military operations against Tehran. Pete Hegseth and Dan Keen were also present, and other topics were discussed.
The audio version 24 with Fardad Farahzad was broadcast live from Jerusalem and covered the ongoing political crisis in Israel.

Kan News Israel reported that the US has transferred 10 transport planes to Israel. These planes moved from Fort Bliss base in Texas to Ovda and Nevatim bases in Israel and likely carry interceptor missiles and air defense equipment. The US also sent other transport planes to Jordan, Saudi Arabia, and Qatar and has close coordination with Israel.

Cristiano Ronaldo scored a hat-trick in the twelfth week of the Saudi Professional League, bringing his career goal tally to 985. Al-Nassr won the match against Al-Kholood 5-3. Ronaldo scored 5 goals in this game, two of which were disallowed.

Jennifer Mortazashvili said forming a national unity government with Netanyahu and opposition parties is more likely than a minority government. She added that despite the increase in Arab party seats, it is unlikely they will have a direct role in the future government. Mortazashvili also said there is no fundamental disagreement between Netanyahu and Gadi Eisenkot on confronting the Islamic Republic, and Israelis are tired of war but consider confronting the Islamic Republic's threats necessary.

Alireza Kiani in episode 17 of "Fereydoun" refers to the patriotism of individuals who claim to be passionate about Iranian history but turn a blind eye to the conflict of the Islamic Republic and its proxy forces with Iranian history.

Alireza Kiani mentioned the widespread migration of Iranian Jews after the 57 catastrophe in episode 17 of "Fereydoun." He questioned how people can take pride in Cyrus the Great's tolerance towards Jews but ignore the Islamic regime's systematic anti-Semitism.

Reuters reported that a hidden network consisting of about five thousand military entities imports equipment and materials needed for the Islamic Republic's missile and drone programs as well as tools of repression into Iran. This network uses trade routes and unconventional methods, including multi-stage shipment transfers and changing purchase and sale invoices, to bring equipment through unofficial channels. Interviews were conducted with Omid Memarian and Masoumeh Taherkhani.

Ben Sabti, a researcher on Iran and Israel, said based on initial assessments, the intervention of Qatar and Turkey in the Israeli elections has not significantly affected the outcome. He pointed to a deadlock in government formation and political disagreements, saying the likelihood of new elections has increased. According to him, the formation of a national unity government involving Benjamin Netanyahu and Gadi Eisenkot may also depend on mediation by Donald Trump.

Reuters reported that a hidden network consisting of about 5,000 covert military entities imports equipment and materials needed for the Islamic Republic's missile and drone programs and repression tools. According to the report, one of these entities managed to bypass sanctions and imported over two billion dollars worth of equipment and goods, including chemical materials used in missile fuel, industrial parts, and heavy trucks, from December 1403 to June 1405. The report includes an interview with Miad Maleki, former head of the US Treasury Department's sanctions targeting office.

Alireza Kiani said in program 17 "Fereydoun" that honoring and respecting Cyrus the Great requires upholding the fundamental rights of Iranians and keeping alive the memory of the January 1404 massacre.

AS reported that Barcelona closed the supporters' section known as "Gol 1957" for the match against Alavés after recording 17 violations in El Clásico. These violations included insults to Mourinho and Cucurella and an attack on Camavinga after Real Madrid's second goal. Barcelona emphasized in its statement that such behaviors could expose the club to financial penalties and even the risk of stadium closure.

Mahmoud Nabavian, a member of the Islamic Republic parliament, announced that during a nighttime gathering of government supporters in Qom, he requested Mojtaba Khamenei to issue a permit for building an atomic bomb. Nabavian wrote on the social network X that he made this request during the gathering and the attendees supported it with Takbir chants.

Yemen's armed forces announced they have received reports of suffocation and unconsciousness cases in Taiz city and are investigating the possibility that the Houthis used shells containing toxic substances in the area. Local officials in Taiz have called for urgent investigations and UN involvement. Yemen's information minister previously stated that the Houthis, with the cooperation of the Islamic Republic, established a factory to produce chemical weapons.

Donald Trump said that the attack on Iran was necessary to prevent the Islamic Republic from obtaining nuclear weapons and emphasized that the war will end soon. He also praised Scott Bassett's performance and said Washington is simultaneously pursuing economic and military pressure against the Islamic Republic. Trump added that Bassett is responsible for advancing economic pressure and that the US is conducting its military operations in an unprecedented manner.

Mike Pompeo, former US Secretary of State, described the US and Israeli military operations against the Islamic Republic as a "100 percent correct" action in an interview with Al Arabiya and said this action was done 7 or even 17 years late. He added that an early military action could have prevented the development of the Islamic Republic's medium-range ballistic missile capabilities. Pompeo had previously supported continued military actions against the Islamic Republic.

According to the Italian Ministry of Defense, an Italian military helicopter operating as part of the EU peacekeeping mission in Bosnia and Herzegovina crashed near Brčko on Thursday, 7 Aban 1405 (2026-10-29), killing four and injuring 11. Two of the deceased were members of the Italian army and two others were members of the Italian Red Cross volunteer military corps. The Italian Ministry of Defense stated that the cause of the crash is under investigation.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations Center (UKMTO) has received a report of an incident 25 nautical miles northeast of Khasab, Oman, in the Strait of Hormuz. A third-party source reported that a ship caught fire while exiting the Strait of Hormuz. The cause of the fire was not known at the time of the report.

Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, announced it is investigating a security incident that may have resulted in the withdrawal of several billion dollars from its wallets. Binance emphasized that user assets are secure and temporarily halted withdrawals on several networks. Changpeng Zhao, founder of Binance, said it appears the exchange has been hacked and expects user assets to be fully reimbursed.

Connecticut Democratic Senator Chris Murphy said he and a number of other US lawmakers were briefed on details of a potential plan to resume military operations against Iran. He described the plan as 'insane' and warned that its implementation would lead to escalation and prolonging of the war. Murphy said the prepared plan would, at Trump's request, prolong the war and have devastating consequences for US security interests.

Scott Bessent, the US Treasury Secretary, said that Washington's economic pressures on the Islamic Republic have reached a stage where Tehran is facing difficulties in securing dollars and paying its military forces. He added that the financial restrictions on the Islamic Republic have also affected Tehran-supported groups, and the financial resources of the Houthis, Hamas, and Hezbollah are being cut off. Bessent emphasized that the US is trying to limit the Islamic Republic's ability to finance these groups.

The office of Prince Reza Pahlavi on X called on democratic countries to expand Iranian people's access to satellite internet and direct satellite-to-mobile phone technology. The office emphasized that democratic countries should invest in this technology to support the Iranian people and guarantee user security. It also noted that Starlink is the last nail in the coffin of government censorship in Iran.

Youssef Raji, Lebanon's Foreign Minister, emphasized that the government's decision to monopolize weapons in the hands of official institutions and expand sovereignty across the country was made to build the state and not to satisfy any foreign party. Joseph Aoun, Lebanon's President, said that safe and sustainable solutions come through diplomatic negotiations, not war. Bishara Charbel, a Lebanese analyst, said the decision to monopolize weapons has broad support, but the government has not shown enough seriousness in implementing it and considered Hezbollah's disarmament a prerequisite for Israel's gradual withdrawal from Lebanon.

Navid Mohibi said Netanyahu lost his previous majority by losing 15 seats, but his opponents have not been able to form a cohesive coalition. Three scenarios are presented for Israel: a national unity government, a minority government supported by Arab parties, or the next election. If parties fail to form a government, Netanyahu can remain as caretaker until the next election.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations reported that a small boat approached an oil tanker in the Strait of Hormuz and attached two explosive devices to its hull, causing a fire and temporary disablement of the tanker. The incident occurred on October 29, 25 nautical miles northeast of Khasab, Oman. The fire has been controlled, all crew are safe, and the tanker is continuing towards the next port.

A Saudi-led military coalition announced it intercepted and destroyed a drone launched by Houthis supported by the Islamic Republic in the Mecca region. Reuters reported that the coalition announced the drone's destruction on Friday, 8 Aban, in a statement. The Houthis have not responded to this incident so far.

Mohammad Qaedi, an international relations lecturer, said that the release of strategic oil reserves by dozens of countries has prevented a further increase in fuel prices in the US in the short term. He emphasized that disruptions in tanker traffic in the Strait of Hormuz continue to threaten the global energy market and a quick return to pre-crisis conditions is unlikely.

Less than a week remains until the US midterm elections; an election that could affect Donald Trump's calculations about the possibility of another attack on the Islamic Republic. Alongside reports about reviewing military options after the elections, the question arises whether Trump will postpone the decision about war until the election results and to what extent a possible Democratic victory in Congress could affect the course of military confrontation with Tehran.

The United States Studies Center at the University of Sydney warned that the Strait of Hormuz crisis poses a long-term threat to the energy security of Australia and Asian countries. The closure of this passage has deprived Asia of 60% of oil supply and 27% of natural gas, increasing energy costs in Southeast Asia by 3.36 billion dollars monthly.
A meeting focused on Cyrus the Great, the heritage of Iranian civilization, and values such as freedom, justice, and human dignity was held in London.

Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, estimated the damage from the recent security breach at about 6.3 billion dollars and announced a temporary halt to deposits and withdrawals. Initial investigations indicate the intrusion likely started through a hacked laptop of one of the company's technical staff.

Behnam Saeedi, a member of the National Security Commission of the Islamic Republic's parliament, said the Islamic Republic has proven it supports its allies, including Hezbollah Lebanon and the resistance axis, to the death, and they will support the Islamic Republic. Saeedi added that the Islamic Republic has shown in its operations that it carries out its threats and that the positions it threatened were targeted. He also said there is still an opportunity for countries to refrain from further cooperation with the US and prevent worsening political and economic damages.

Reuters reported on Friday, 8 Aban, quoting an informed official that Qatari mediators returned to Tehran as part of efforts to reach an agreement between the Islamic Republic and the United States. The official also said that the Qatari mediation talks were conducted with coordination from the United States.

In the NBA, the Portland Trail Blazers suffered their first loss of the season against the Memphis Grizzlies. The New Orleans Pelicans achieved their first win of the season with strong performances from their bench players. The Atlanta Hawks ended the Cleveland Cavaliers' winning streak.

Ali Shirazi, a member of Iran International's editorial board, said that the request by parliament members and supporters of the Islamic Republic from Mojtaba Khamenei to authorize the construction of an atomic bomb is both an effort to distract the regime's supporters and a message to the US and Israel ahead of possible attacks; a message indicating that the Islamic Republic has not yet pursued building a bomb.

Israel Hayom newspaper reported, citing American and diplomatic officials, that the resumption of attacks against the Islamic Republic does not depend on the formation of a new government in Israel, and Washington and Israel continue their military, intelligence, and political coordination to decide on next steps. A senior US government official said Washington intends to eliminate the threats of the Islamic Republic in the remaining two years of Donald Trump's presidency and facilitate new regional agreements in the Middle East. This official warned that Israeli leaders must seize this opportunity, otherwise the war for Israel's survival will be much harder.

On Thursday, 7 Aban 1405, six Sunni citizens were arrested in the city of Shavur by the Intelligence Forces of the IRGC. The identities of five of them, Hossein Navaseri, Ali Doshi, Ali Shuyehi, Amin Shuyehi, and Javad Kanani, have been confirmed. These arrests were made without a judicial warrant at around 1:30 AM.

A 38-year-old man in Tehran who deceived a 27-year-old woman with the promise of finding a job and sexually assaulted her was arrested by intelligence police officers. The suspect confessed to the crime after arrest and was transferred to prison with the issuance of a temporary detention order.

According to information received by Iran International, Abdullah Abdollahi, a retired Quran and religious education teacher in Aliabad, ended his life after his young daughter was arrested during a birthday party and judicial authorities insisted on continuing her detention. Nahal Abdollahi, about 25 years old, had invited about 30 to 40 friends to the newly established and luxurious Atlan Hotel in Aliabad for her birthday last week, where police officers entered undercover and arrested about 30 participants. Nahal Abdollahi remains held in Amirabad prison, and her father's efforts to secure her release have been unsuccessful.

Ali Salehi, the public and revolutionary prosecutor of Tehran, called the content published by some tourist tours on social networks "immoral" and an example of "norm violation" and ordered that pages of unlicensed tourist tours be identified and blocked within one week. He demanded legal action against the operators of these pages and increased supervision over public places including sports halls and restaurants. Salehi warned that in case of "norm violation," legal action will be taken not only against the offender but also against the license issuer.

Fatemeh Heydari, Director General of Women's and Family Affairs of Qom Province, announced the launch of a campaign in which stores are asked to offer their products with discounts as a form of "vow" on the occasion of Fatemeh Zahra's birthday. She introduced this initiative as part of programs to strengthen "Islamic identity" against the spread of occasions like Halloween and Black Friday in Iran. Coordination with the municipality and cultural organizations of Qom has been made to implement these programs on a larger scale.

Sardar Azmoun, Iranian forward of Shabab Al Ahli UAE, said after his team's 2-0 victory over Esteghlal that the coach's trust and teammates' support helped him return to his brilliant days after overcoming injuries. In an interview with Al Emarat Al Youm newspaper, he spoke about his strong mindset to face challenges. Azmoun also emphasized the role of Andre Jardine, the Brazilian coach, in his comeback.
